conviction_note: abs_move 18 (the option-implied 18.35% event move, beside a 12% median and a 52% max in the name's own history); p_up 53, a faint lean up from a crowded and rising short (16.8% of float, 7 days to cover), a beat-the-guide record (Q1 +2.9% over the top of the range, Q2 at the top) and a guide that excludes the Salesforce rollout announced on 2026-09-15. The lean is pulled toward 50 because this name sold a surcharge-driven beat by -29% last quarter and the skew pays for downside. The findings sum to +3.4, about three times the scaled +1.08: the sum counts each small positive in full, while p_up nets them against the reaction-function risk.
bar: Company Q3 2026 guide: revenue $231-235m, adjusted EBITDA $32-34m, non-GAAP EPS $0.45-0.49; FY2026 revenue $900-910m, adj. EBITDA $123-125m, non-GAAP EPS $1.71-1.79 (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1514416/000151441626000055/q220268kexh991.htm, 2026-07-29). FY cloud communications guide $622-626m from the Q2 call (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978137-20260808). Sell-side Q3 revenue consensus was not found from two agreeing sources. Pre-guide consensus was $223.6m / $0.40 (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/bandwidth-q2-earnings-top-estimates-strong-ai-driven-demand), and Benzinga still shows $0.40 EPS. So the bar is the company guide, with $233m / $0.47 at the midpoint. Implied Q4 revenue is about $238-248m (FY guide less Q1 $208.8m, Q2 $219.9m and a Q3 midpoint of $233m).
positioning_check: Short interest is 5,117,810 shares, 16.79% of float, 7.0 days to cover, as of the 2026-10-15 record date (FINRA, published 2026-10-26). That is up 8.4% from 4,723,069 on 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/BAND/short-interest/). In March 2026 it was about 1.17m shares and 2.3 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/band/shortinterest), so the short has roughly quadrupled. Sealed baseline: skew_25d +4.16 vol points (downside paid, moderate), put/call open-interest ratio 0.36 (call-heavy), ATM spread 36% of mid. Tape: spot $50, 20d -17.6%, 5d +6.8%, 36% below the 52-week high, 290% above the 52-week low, 20d realised vol 99%. This is a crowded and rising short into a print on a name that has moved +52% and -29% on its last two releases.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 8.4% in the last fortnight to 5.12m shares, 16.8% of float and 7.0 days to cover (2026-10-15 record date, published 2026-10-26), about 4x the ~1.17m of March 2026. The build came into a 17.6% 20-day drawdown, including an unexplained -8.8% on 2026-10-08 and a thin-volume -14.3% intraday print on 2026-10-22. Against that, call open interest is about 3x put open interest (P/C 0.36).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline shows +52.1% on 2026-04-30, when a Q1 beat over the top of the guide met a de-rated stock, and -29.3% on 2026-07-29, when a beat met a stock that had run up 277% over twelve months. Short interest at those dates is not on file, but the March 2026 reading was 1.17m shares.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is a public number. The point is that the short is near its high exactly when the stock has given back 36% from its high, so the downside case is already partly in the price and in the short. If the market expected a squeeze, the 20-day trend would not be -17.6% and the skew would not be put-paid. The +6.8% five-day bounce may be early covering.
findings.independence: Drawdown evidence: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-bandwidth-nasdaq-band-stock-falls-88-whats-next-2026-10-08/ and https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-bandwidth-nasdaq-band-stock-price-down-143-heres-why-2026-10-22/ (no cause given; the 10-22 move was on volume about 90% below average). Call-heavy open interest comes from the sealed baseline (Yahoo options), a different source from FINRA.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is likely at or above the $235m top of the guide, but mostly through pass-through surcharges. Bandwidth beat its own guide in Q1 (actual $208.8m against $200-203m) and landed at the top in Q2 ($219.9m against $214-220m). Q3 is the first quarter carrying full-period carrier surcharge increases: AT&T 10DLC SMS $0.0030 to $0.0035 and MMS $0.0075 to $0.0090 from 2026-04-01, and T-Mobile 10DLC $0.003 to $0.004 from 2026-01-19. Surcharge revenue already rose from about $59m in Q1 to $68m in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue at the top of the guide, partly from surcharges, and the stock fell 29.3% because the beat was read as pass-through and low quality (https://www.financialcontent.com/article/stockstory-2026-7-29-why-bandwidth-band-stock-is-nosediving). Q1 2026: a 2.9% beat over the top of the guide, and the stock rose 52.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Management knew the surcharge schedule when it guided on 2026-07-29, so most of this sits inside the $231-235m guide. Any upside is a beat on total revenue, not on cloud communications, and that is the line the market discounts. If the market priced a quality beat, there would be no 17% drawdown into the print.
findings.independence: T-Mobile fee change: https://support.twilio.com/hc/en-us/articles/44609260499995-T-Mobile-Messaging-Carrier-Fee-Changes-January-2026. Guide-beat record: the Q4 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1514416/000151441626000014/q420258kexh991.htm) and the Q2 release. All are primary documents.

findings.finding: The line that sank Q2 is gross margin quality. GAAP gross margin fell to 36% from 40% on surcharges, and FY non-GAAP EPS was trimmed to $1.71-1.79 from $1.77-1.83 for infrastructure investment. Morgan Stanley's initiation (2026-10-16, Equal-weight, $56 target) puts gross profit on incremental cloud revenue at about 68% in Q2 2026, against 82% in FY2025. Management guided non-GAAP gross margin up in Q3-Q4 to about 60% for the year (Q2: 59.4%), and its Q3 EPS guide of $0.45-0.49 implies a step-up from Q2's $0.37.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-29: gross margin down 4.1 points year on year and the FY EPS trim drove a -29.3% day despite a raised revenue guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The concern is in the wire, so it is partly priced. What is not priced is the sign of the Q3 incremental margin: management committed to expansion, while MS shows the incremental trend going the other way. A print that confirms ~60% would remove the bear case, and one below 59% would repeat Q2. Net sign is slightly negative because the name has punished margin quality before.
findings.independence: Primary: Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1514416/000151441626000055/q220268kexh991.htm), GAAP 36% against 40% and non-GAAP 59% against 58%. Management's ~60% FY target is from the call transcript (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978137-20260808). Two documents, one concern.

findings.finding: Guidance setup. The FY cloud communications guide of $622-626m (about 11% growth) explicitly 'left out ... any future benefit related to Salesforce', and management said 'there's some conservatism in our model' (Q2 call, 2026-07-29). On 2026-09-15, after that guide, Bandwidth announced it is the first certified carrier for the global rollout of Salesforce's native Contact Center across 25+ countries 'this fall', via BYOC on Maestro. The same day it filed an investor deck (8-K 7.01) reiterating '20% revenue growth and 33% Adjusted EBITDA growth for 2026'. The FY revenue guide has been raised twice ($864-884m to $880-900m to $900-910m). Implied Q4 is about $238-248m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raised FY guides: +52.1% in April 2026 (raise with a beat) and -29.3% in July 2026 (revenue raised, EPS trimmed, H2 cloud deceleration flagged). The guide is the line this stock trades on, in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: The Salesforce expansion was announced and the stock still fell from about $61 at end-September to $50, so the market is not paying for a raise. The guide excludes Salesforce by management's own statement. If a raise were priced, the 20-day trend and the put-paid skew would look different. Morgan Stanley's EW and BofA's Neutral show the sell-side is not underwriting upside either.
findings.independence: Salesforce release: https://finviz.com/news/392175/bandwidth-and-salesforce-expand-collaboration-to-support-the-global-rollout-of-salesforces-native-contact-center. Guide exclusion and 'conservatism' quotes: https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978137-20260808 (separate document). Piper Sandler estimates the voice-only Agentforce opportunity at +2-3 points of growth in 2027-28 (via the MS article).

findings.finding: Peer read after Bandwidth last spoke: Twilio's Q2 release on 2026-08-06 raised its FY2026 organic growth guide to 13-13.5% from 9.5-10.5%, with dollar-based net expansion of 116% (108% a year earlier). That points to strong CPaaS and voice/agent demand through mid-2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved history on peer read-throughs for this name. Bandwidth's own commercial net retention rose to 113% (+3 points q/q) in Q2.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, has been available for 12 weeks and was surely seen. It is filed because it postdates Bandwidth's guide and supports a cloud-revenue beat. Bandwidth's 17% 20-day decline suggests the market is not extrapolating it.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Twilio is a competitor, not a counterparty, and its Q3 2026 print had not been released as of 2026-10-28.

findings.finding: Political messaging: FY2026 political revenue was cut to $13m from $15m, with about $1m in Q2 and the rest 'principally in the second half'. Local reports through mid-October describe surging midterm texting (e.g. Alaska on 2026-10-15; Oklahoma at '10,000 texts per hour' in July). No 2026 volume count was found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Political revenue was $46m in the twelve months to June 2025 and $3m in the twelve months to June 2026 (investor deck slide 9). No resolved reaction history isolates this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The company lowered the political number, so the bar is conservative. At $13m on a ~$905m year the line is small, and even a 50% overshoot is about $6m, roughly 1% of H2 revenue.
findings.independence: Proxy, anecdotal: https://www.fox13news.com/news/political-texts-surging-2026-here-how-reduce. The $13m comes from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978137-20260808).

findings.finding: Capital return capacity. The credit agreement's third amendment (effective 2026-07-25) doubled the annual restricted-payment cap to $40m (or 20% of TTM EBITDA). About $60m of the $80m buyback authorization remained at 2026-06-30. In August the company repurchased $20.8m principal of its 2028 converts at a discount, leaving only $6.7m outstanding. The Q3 print will disclose any buyback at depressed prices.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction. The $80m program was announced with the Q4 2025 print (+11.9% day, alongside other news).
findings.why_not_priced: The covenant change sits in an 8-K item 1.01 that no preview mentions. The Q3 buyback amount is unknown until the release. Size is small because $40m a year is about 2.5% of a ~$1.5bn market cap.
findings.independence: Convert repurchase 8-K 8.01: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1514416/000151441626000060/0001514416-26-000060.txt (separate document). Remaining authorization per the Q2 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001514416/000151441626000057/band-20260630.htm.

findings.finding: Director Lukas Roush sold 1,500 shares at $49.04 on 2026-10-16 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-05-28. His Form 144 covers 4,500 shares and he holds 58,769 after the sale. An insider Form 144 cluster on 2026-08-27 was followed by Form 4s on 2026-09-01 to 09-03.
findings.why_not_priced: The plan was pre-scheduled and the sale is tiny. It carries almost no information, which is why it is sized near zero.

outside_window.finding: The $13m of 2026 political revenue does not recur in 2027 (flagged in Morgan Stanley's 2026-10-16 initiation). This is a headwind to the 2027 cloud growth rate, and the formal 2027 guide normally comes with the Q4 print in February.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The faint upward lean runs against the put-paid skew (+4.16) but with the call-heavy open interest, the crowded and rising short and the -17.6% 20-day de-rating. The name sold a pass-through-driven beat by 29% last quarter, which keeps p_up close to 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the reported-quarter revenue-beat finding cut from +0.8 to +0.4, because this name sold a surcharge-driven top-of-guide beat by -29% last quarter. p_up moved from 54 to 53.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest had already been looked up. The 16.8% float short supports the positive positioning finding, so it was left at +1.0 and not enlarged.
Lesson 5 (proxy against document): the Twilio peer finding and the political finding stay small and are labelled as proxies; nothing changed.
Lesson 6 (bar): the bar is the company guide (a primary document), so no cap applied. The one out-of-window item (the 2027 political non-recurrence) was already in outside_window.
